sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 所以我们自称为一个移民国家，

sentences.en: one of the first German language newspapers in the colonies.

sentences.en: Indeed, the first border patrol consisted of only a couple dozen men on horseback.
sentences.zh: 事实上，第一支边境巡逻队仅由骑马的几十个人组成。

sentences.en: So when someone says to me, my ancestors immigrated legally, why can't they?
sentences.zh: 所以当有人对我说，我的祖先是合法移民，为什么现在的移民不能合法前来？

sentences.en: My first question is, when did your ancestors immigrate?
sentences.zh: 我的第一个问题是，你的祖先是什么时候移民的？

sentences.en: Because if they immigrated in the 19th century or in the early 20th century, they simply didn't use that vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们在19世纪或20世纪初移民，他们根本不会使用那种词汇。

sentences.en: They didn't think in those terMs.
sentences.zh: 他们不会用那些术语去思考。

sentences.en: So clearly, much of the language around immigration has changed over time.
sentences.zh: 很显然，随着时间的推移，许多关于移民的语言都发生了变化。

sentences.en: But there are also ideas that have remained relatively constant.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些观点相对保持不变。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'll ask Maria Cristina about the long and tangled relationship between immigration and national security.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我将向玛丽亚·克里斯蒂娜请教移民与国家安全之间漫长而纠葛的关系。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Our debates over immigration are often framed in the context of national security, fears of terrorism.
sentences.zh: 我们关于移民的辩论往往是在国家安全和对恐怖主义的恐惧的背景下展开的。

sentences.en: To many of us, this feels relatively new, part of the 9-11 world we've lived in over the past 15 years.
sentences.zh: 对我们很多人来说，这感觉相对较新，是我们过去15年来所经历的9·11世界的一部分。

sentences.en: But Maria Cristina Garcia says that if we look at history,
sentences.zh: 但玛丽亚·克里斯蒂娜·加西亚表示，如果我们回顾历史，
zh_words: 玛丽亚·克里斯蒂娜·加西亚

sentences.en: we start to see that our modern concerns are a new version of a story that's been told over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我们就会开始发现，我们现代的担忧其实是一场不断重演的故事的新版本。

sentences.en: Americans have been concerned about national security since the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 自19世纪以来，美国人就一直对国家安全感到担忧。

sentences.en: One has only to look at the political cartoons of Thomas Nast, for example,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，只要看看托马斯·纳斯特的政治漫画，

sentences.en: to see how concerned Americans were about Irish Catholics, for example.
sentences.zh: 就能看出当年美国人对爱尔兰天主教徒是多么担忧。

sentences.en: Thomas Nast produced these political cartoons warning Americans about all these Catholics
sentences.zh: 托马斯·纳斯特创作了这些政治漫画，警告美国人注意所有这些天主教徒，

sentences.en: who are coming to the United States, who were under the influence of the Vatican,
sentences.zh: 他们来到美国，受到梵蒂冈的影响，

sentences.en: who didn't understand democratic principles and would undermine democratic institutions.
sentences.zh: 不理解民主原则，并且会破坏民主制度。

sentences.en: And so that's an early example of Americans concerned about national security.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是美国人关注国家安全的一个早期例子。

sentences.en: In the late 19th century, you see Americans expressing great concern about all the Southern and Eastern Europeans
sentences.zh: 在19世纪后期，你会发现美国人对所有来自南欧和东欧的人表达了极大的担忧，

sentences.en: Americans who are coming in who are anarchists and Bolsheviks and socialists who don't understand,
sentences.zh: 那些涌入美国的、被称为无政府主义者、布尔什维克和社会主义者的美国新移民，他们不理解——

sentences.en: again, don't understand American democracy, will undermine American principles, American democratic institutions.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，他们不理解美国民主，会破坏美国的原则和美国的民主制度。

sentences.en: And this concern is strong enough that it forces Congress to pass a series of quota laws barring immigration from Southern and Eastern Europe.
sentences.zh: 这种担忧如此强烈，以至于迫使国会通过了一系列配额法，禁止来自南欧和东欧的移民。

sentences.en: We see concerns about the Chinese and other Asian groups.
sentences.zh: 我们也能看到对中国人和其它亚洲群体的担忧。

sentences.en: So we see that concern about national security throughout American history.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在整个美国历史中都能看到这种对国家安全的担忧。

sentences.en: Americans may not have used the exact term national security in the 19th century,
sentences.zh: 美国人在19世纪可能没有使用过“国家安全”这个确切的词，

sentences.en: but you see those concerns all throughout the history.
sentences.zh: 但你在整个历史中都能看到这些担忧。

sentences.en: I want to spend a little bit of time talking about the World War II period
sentences.zh: 我想花一点时间聊聊二战时期

sentences.en: and the experience of Japanese Americans in the United States,
sentences.zh: 以及日裔美国人在美国的经历，

sentences.en: because it seems like that's certainly a moment where concerns about security
sentences.zh: 因为那似乎确实是一个这样的时刻：对安全的担忧

sentences.en: and concerns about loyalty to the United States intersected with how we were thinking about an immigrant group.
sentences.zh: 与对美国忠诚的担忧，同我们看待一个移民群体的方式交织在了一起。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: During periods of national emergency, immigrants become likely scapegoats.
sentences.zh: 在国家紧急状态期间，移民往往会成为替罪羊。

sentences.en: We saw this during World War II with the internment of Japanese immigrants,
sentences.zh: 我们在二战期间拘禁日本移民时看到了这一点，

sentences.en: but also their American-born children who, even though there was no evidence that Japanese or their children
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，还有他们在美国出生的孩子——尽管没有任何证据表明日本移民或他们的孩子

sentences.en: were conspiring against the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在密谋反对美国

sentences.en: government or against American society,
sentences.zh: 政府或美国社会，

sentences.en: the government decided to err on the side of caution and rounded up this population
sentences.zh: 但政府为了保险起见，还是把这群人抓起来，

sentences.en: and put them in internment camps.
sentences.zh: 关进了拘禁营。

sentences.en: It was one of the most shameful periods in American history.
sentences.zh: 这是美国历史上最耻辱的时期之一。

sentences.en: Those who were interned and their children felt the consequences of that executive decision
sentences.zh: 那些被拘禁的人及其子女在之后的几十年里，

sentences.en: for many, many decades afterwards.
sentences.zh: 一直承受着那个行政决定的后果。

sentences.en: And so that's just one example.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是一个例子。

sentences.en: But also during World War II, there were many opportunities that we lost to accommodate people fleeing Europe.
sentences.zh: 但在二战期间，我们也失去了许多接纳逃离欧洲之人的机会。

sentences.en: And we lost that opportunity because we feared – again, we were concerned with national security.
sentences.zh: 我们失去了这个机会，是因为我们害怕——再次说明，我们当时关心的是国家安全。

sentences.en: We feared that among the refugees, among the immigrants,
sentences.zh: 我们担心在难民和移民当中，

sentences.en: would be spies and saboteurs that would undermine the United States.
sentences.zh: 会混有破坏美国的间谍和破坏分子。

sentences.en: But those fears prevented us from accommodating many, many people who were fleeing the Third Reich
sentences.zh: 正是这些恐惧阻止我们接纳许许多多正逃离第三帝国

sentences.en: and needed protection.
sentences.zh: 且需要保护的人。

sentences.en: And we lost that opportunity to help them.
sentences.zh: 我们失去了帮助他们的机会。

sentences.en: When you look at the experience of Jewish immigrants and refugees around the time of World War II,
sentences.zh: 当你回顾二战前后（大约20世纪30、40年代）犹太移民和难民的经历时，

sentences.en: around the 1930s, 1940s, paint me a picture of what happened.
sentences.zh: 请为我描述一下当时的情况。

sentences.en: The popular narrative is that there were many European Jews who did make it to the United States,
sentences.zh: 流行的说法是，有许多欧洲犹太人确实成功来到了美国，

sentences.en: many of whom were involved in the scientific research that had helped the United States eventually win World War II.
sentences.zh: 其中许多人参与了帮助美国最终赢得二战的科学研究。

sentences.en: But was that sort of a general experience?
sentences.zh: 但那算是一种普遍的经历吗？

sentences.en: Was the United States generally welcoming to Jewish refugees from Europe in the middle of the 20th century?
sentences.zh: 在20世纪中叶，美国总体上欢迎来自欧洲的犹太难民吗？

sentences.en: No, we weren't, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，并没有。

sentences.en: Many historians feel that our policies were highly anti-Semitic during this period.
sentences.zh: 许多历史学家认为，我们在此期间的政策具有高度的反犹太主义色彩。

sentences.en: We lost many opportunities to allow Jewish refugees to come to the United States.
sentences.zh: 我们失去了许多允许犹太难民来到美国的机会。

sentences.en: The most classic example is the SS St. Louis, a ship carrying over 900 passengers who were fleeing Europe.
sentences.zh: 最典型的例子就是“圣路易斯号”客轮，船上载有900多名逃离欧洲的乘客。

sentences.en: And when they arrived off the American coast, the people on the ship were prevented from coming to the United States.
sentences.zh: 当他们抵达美国海岸时，船上的人被阻止进入美国。

sentences.en: The ship was turned away.
sentences.zh: 这艘船被驱逐了。

sentences.en: And eventually, you know, the ship traveled to many different countries.
sentences.zh: 最后，你知道的，这艘船去了许多不同的国家。

sentences.en: They were also denied the opportunity to land.
sentences.zh: 他们也被拒绝登陆。

sentences.en: And eventually, the ship was forced to return to Europe.
sentences.zh: 最终，这艘船被迫返回欧洲。

sentences.en: And many of the people who were traveling on the SS St. Louis eventually were caught and sent to camps, to the death camps.
sentences.zh: “圣路易斯号”上的许多乘客最终被抓住并送往了集中营、死亡营。

sentences.en: So when we look at the broad sweep of history here, we sort of see this pattern repeatedly occurring where groups arrive.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们审视这段漫长厚重的历史时，我们会发现这种模式在不断重演：群体不断到来。

sentences.en: And within a few decades or a couple of generations of being here, they have concerns about newcomers entering their neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 而在他们来到这里几十年或两代人之后，他们又开始担心新来者进入他们的社区。

sentences.en: And, you know, in some ways, we seem to have a positive view of immigration and immigrants when they were long ago and far away, but less so when they're here now, when, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，在某种程度上，当移民是很久以前、很远的事情时，我们似乎对移民和难民抱有积极的看法；但当他们现在就来到这里时，比如，你知道的，

sentences.en: the family that arrived last year that lives next door.
sentences.zh: 去年搬来住在隔壁的那个家庭，这种看法就没那么积极了。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering if you have insight into why this happens.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你对这种现象的原因有什么见解。

sentences.en: Why is it that groups that themselves may have faced challenges as immigrants, how is it that within a couple of decades or maybe a couple of generations,
sentences.zh: 为什么那些作为移民本身可能也面临过挑战的群体，在短短几十年甚至两代人的时间里，

sentences.en: they are turning around and having the same concerns that were expressed about them not so long ago?
sentences.zh: 就会转过头来，表现出不久前别人对他们所表达过的那些担忧？

sentences.en: Well, that seems to be the pattern.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这似乎就是规律。

sentences.en: I guess you could say that part of Americanization is to adopt the values and the perspectives of the society that surrounds you.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以这样说：美国化的一部分就是采纳你周围社会的价值观和视角。

sentences.en: And it also becomes a defense mechanism.
sentences.zh: 这也变成了一种防御机制。

sentences.en: It becomes a way of proving your membership in the society to adopt those values and to reflect those values out to demonstrate that you are a member of the in group and not the out group.
sentences.zh: 它成了一种证明你融入该社会的方式：采纳那些价值观，并将其折射出来，以证明你是这个内群体的一员，而不是外群体。

sentences.en: You recently wrote an essay about the current debates over immigration in which you said,
sentences.zh: 你最近写了一篇关于当前移民辩论的文章，其中你提到：

sentences.en: Generations from now, students in U.S.
sentences.zh: 几代人之后，美国

sentences.en: history classes, many of them the children of immigrants arriving today, will read what our political candidates, editorialists, bloggers,
sentences.zh: 历史课上的学生——其中许多人是今天抵达的移民的子女——在读到我们的政治候选人、社论作家、博主

sentences.en: and talking heads had to say about their ancestors and shudder.
sentences.zh: 以及电视名嘴对他们的祖先的评价时，会感到不寒而栗。

sentences.en: What did you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: When I teach courses in immigration history and we read the editorials and the newspaper articles and the broadsides that were published in the 19th and in the early 20th century,
sentences.zh: 当我教授移民史课程，而我们阅读19世纪和20世纪初出版的社论、报纸文章和檄文时，

sentences.en: My students often shake their heads and wonder how Americans could have ever had those feelings or those thoughts or perspectives.
sentences.zh: 我的大学生们经常摇头，纳闷美国人怎么会有那些感受、想法或视角。

sentences.en: They laugh nervously.
sentences.zh: 他们紧张地笑着。

sentences.en: But then when we compare those editorials and newspaper articles and broadsides to some of the editorials and blogs and newspaper articles today, they see the continuities.
sentences.zh: 但随后，当我们把这些社论、报纸文章和檄文与当今的一些社论、博客和报纸文章进行比较时，他们看到了连贯性。

sentences.en: And so I suspect that 20 years from now, 30 years from now, I suspect that my students reading the thoughts, the articles of today will also find them ridiculous,
sentences.zh: 所以我猜，20年后、30年后，我的学生们在阅读今天的想法和文章时，也会觉得它们荒谬，

sentences.en: will also shudder, will also wonder why Americans felt the way they did.
sentences.zh: 也会感到不寒而栗，也会纳闷为什么当年的美国人会有那种感受。

sentences.en: But I hope not.
sentences.zh: 但我希望不会。

sentences.en: There's this part of me that hopes that we will do better, that we will be better.
sentences.zh: 我内心深处有一种期望，希望我们能做得更好，希望我们能变得更好。

sentences.en: That was historian Maria Cristina Garcia.
sentences.zh: 以上采访的是历史学家玛丽亚·克里斯蒂娜·加西亚。
zh_words: 玛丽亚·克里斯蒂娜·加西亚

sentences.en: She's a professor of American Studies at Cornell University.
sentences.zh: 她是康奈尔大学的美国研究教授。

sentences.en: Hidden Brain is produced by Jenny Schmidt, Maggie Penman, Raina Cohen, Rene Klar, and Parth Shah.
sentences.zh: 《隐藏的大脑》由珍妮·施密特、玛吉·佩恩曼、莱娜·科恩、勒内·克拉尔和帕思·沙阿制作。

sentences.en: Our supervising producer is Tara Boyle.
sentences.zh: 我们的主管制作人是塔拉·博伊尔。

sentences.en: This week, our unsung hero is Stuart Harding.
sentences.zh: 本周我们的无名英雄是斯图尔特·哈丁。

sentences.en: Stuart's one of NPR's lawyers.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特是NPR的律师之一。

sentences.en: He does many things for us, from working late on a Friday to draft the rules for a t-shirt giveaway,
sentences.zh: 他为我们做了很多事情，从周五加班起草T恤赠送活动的规则，

sentences.en: to writing the contracts for actors who will appear in an upcoming episode of the show.
sentences.zh: 到为将要出现在本节目未来剧集中的演员撰写合同。

sentences.en: Thank you, Stuart, for all that you do for us, and all that you do for everyone at NPR.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，斯图尔特，感谢你为我们所做的一切，以及你为NPR所有人所做的一切。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆，这里是NPR。

sentences.en: Thank you, Stuart, for hours, and viewers.
sentences.zh: 感谢斯图尔特付出的时间和观众的支持。

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待。
